title: What DARPA Taught Me About Building Trust into Silicon
gist: A Rambus CAD engineer who worked on DARPA's AISS program argues commercial chip design still treats hardware security as a late manual checklist. He says it should be an optimizer variable (PASS: Power, Area, Speed, Security) backed by red teams, explicit boot-trust assumptions and untrusted treatment of AI-generated RTL. The author is Sajeed Mohammad; the raw record lists 'Admin'.

insights.claim: DARPA's AISS (Automatic Implementation of Secure Silicon) program set a target of cutting the time from architecture to security-hardened RTL from years to weeks.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Government funding is pushing hardware security toward automated tooling, a potential demand driver for security-aware EDA.
insights.locator: What the program was actually trying to do

insights.claim: AISS started from the premise that most of today's chips are largely unprotected because hardware security has been a manual craft practiced by a few experts at the largest companies, with no common tools in wide use.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Implies a wide market gap for automated hardware-security tooling and IP.
insights.locator: AISS started from an uncomfortable premise

insights.claim: AISS organized around four attack surfaces (side-channel attacks, reverse engineering, supply-chain attacks such as overproduction, remarking and recycled parts, and malicious hardware) and answered with security-aware CAD tools, security IP libraries, generators and cloud lifecycle management.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Provides a checklist of the hardware threat categories and tooling areas to monitor for vendor activity.
insights.locator: The program organized around four major attack surfaces

themes.theme: Security as a PASS optimization axis

insights.claim: AISS targeted SoC platforms optimized across four axes (Power, Area, Speed and Security, abbreviated PASS) rather than the usual three, promoting security from a sign-off checklist to a variable the optimizer trades off.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: If adopted, EDA vendors that build security into the optimizer could differentiate their flows.
insights.locator: The output would be SoC platforms optimized across four axes

insights.claim: In most production flows security arrives as an end-of-flow gate after the architecture is frozen, so each fix costs about an order of magnitude more than it would have six months earlier.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Late-stage security fixes add schedule and cost risk to tapeouts, which favors shift-left tooling.
insights.locator: 1. Put security in the optimizer, not the checklist

insights.claim: AISS made lifecycle security concrete with odometers (lifecycle counters so a recycled part cannot be sold as new), watermarks proving provenance, and power-on authentication as the first handshake between silicon and the world.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Chip identity and lifecycle tracking are emerging features to watch in counterfeit and supply-chain security.
insights.locator: The program's vocabulary shows how concrete this got

insights.claim: AISS funded a dedicated independent verification red team to attack every mitigation, and all performers joined a two-day quarterly review where the red team demoed what it had broken.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Standing adversarial review is the model the author wants commercial teams to copy.
insights.locator: And DARPA does not grade its own homework

insights.claim: On-chip performance monitoring units (PMUs), debug counters designers trust and ignore, can be repurposed as oracles that leak secrets through power signatures, even though nothing about the PMU is functionally wrong.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Functional correctness does not imply security; debug and monitoring blocks are an overlooked attack surface in SoCs.

insights.claim: Commercial teams that cannot afford a standing red team can put someone in every design review whose job is to break the design rather than confirm it, treating threat modeling as a habit rather than a pre-tapeout document.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A low-cost process change that security-conscious chip teams can adopt.
insights.quote: Threat modeling is not a document you write before tapeout. It is a habit.

insights.claim: A security engine is the component everything else trusts, so it must establish trust in itself from a cold start with no one to vouch for it, and writing its boot requirements forces teams to list every assumption in the boot chain.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Unlisted boot-chain assumptions are potential vulnerabilities; vendors and customers should demand them be documented.
insights.locator: 3. You have to boot trust from nothing

insights.claim: Commercial firmware teams live with dozens of unverified trust assumptions because enumerating them is tedious, and attackers enumerate them for free after release.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Post-release exposure of boot-chain assumptions is a latent liability for chip and device makers.
insights.quote: Attackers enumerate them for you, for free, after release.
insights.locator: 3. You have to boot trust from nothing

insights.claim: Commercial EDA flows still optimize three axes, and security checklists were written for human-written RTL, so AI-generated blocks can inherit blind spots from training data and prompts with no checklist covering them.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: AI-assisted chip design creates a new unaddressed security surface and a possible product opening for verification tools.
insights.locator: Where the commercial world is behind

insights.claim: The author recommends treating AI-generated RTL as untrusted input until it passes the same adversarial review given to third-party IP, and asking EDA vendors which security properties their flow constructs automatically versus merely checks.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Useful diligence questions for EDA vendors and chip design teams adopting AI design tools.
insights.quote: The difference is the whole game.
insights.locator: What to do on Monday morning
